summary: This one is worth running and needs no companions. The gate-widened kernel at _num_splits depth has already been measured (sliding-single-launch-fused-attention: 23.87 / 38.47 us at S=4 / S=2), so a single S=16 run on decode_16 and decode_32 shows what split depth does on its own, and the per-shape result can be read whether it wins or loses.
justification: The mechanism is plausible. At sliding decode with M=16 query rows (G=8, L=1) and page_size 1, each program's old-key loop is a chain of dependent loads that miss a cold L2: a page-table load, then a gather of 64-byte K/V rows, for every 64-key tile. Each extra serial tile costs about one DRAM latency pair. The decode_16 and decode_32 bytes (8 / 16 MB, floors 1.6 / 3.3 us) are far below the measured times, so the time is latency and concurrency, not bandwidth. There are three data points: B=1/S=16/2 tiles at 13.5 us, B=16/S=4/8 tiles at 23.9 us and B=32/S=2/16 tiles at 38.5 us. They fit about 1.5-1.8 us per extra tile. Going to 512 or 1024 CTAs with 2 tiles each raises the bytes in flight per SM about 4-8x, which is what a latency-bound gather needs. The expected numbers are consistent with TASK.md weights. Taking sliding decode_16 from 20.66 to ~13 us saves ~350 us on a 3461 us load (~1.11x). Taking decode_32 from 24.89 to ~14.5 us saves ~480 us on a 5921 us load (~1.08-1.09x). That gives ~1.03x geomean, which should clear the +/-1.5% CI and best's CI high (1.321) only narrowly. decode_1 is byte-identical (_num_splits(1,2) already returns 16) and verify stays on FA3, so the flat predictions are sound. Weakest link: in the three data points, tiles per program, grid size and total bytes all change together with B. The data therefore does not show that the ~10.5 us fixed cost at B=1 (32 CTAs) stays fixed at 512-1024 CTAs. At B=32 the grid is 1024 CTAs of 4 warps, and with num_stages=2 dot tiles (~16-32 KB smem each) that is about 7 resident per SM on 132 SMs. A partial second wave, or 64 combines each reading 16 x 4 KB partials, could push decode_32 to 16-18 us, still a win but a smaller one. A secondary concern is that verify_1 at S=16 (2 tiles, M=64) took 42 us. Something other than tile count clearly costs a lot in this kernel, possibly the M-tile size. That does not apply to M=16 decode, but it is a reminder that the tile-count model does not cover everything.
confounders: sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate: this is the code being widened, not a confounder. B=1 keeps S=16 and its path is byte-identical, so the decode_1 result stays as landed. A merge with the queued sliding-fused-triton-decode1-splits-32 (B=1 only) would touch the same split-count line in _sliding_forward. Keep the edit to a `16 if length == 1 else _num_splits(...)` form so a 3-way merge stays clean.

fused-preattention-triton: the incumbent's sliding decode_16/32 time includes its 1.7-1.9 us _pre_attention_kernel launch. Folding it into the fused kernel is part of the intended gain, not an interaction. Its full-layer and verify use is unchanged.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing / paired-heads-launch-cleanup / paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate: full layers only (window == 0). The sliding path never reads the paired layout, so there is no shared launch sequence, memory traffic or numerical path.
interference: No companion is warranted. The control that isolates sub-change (1), the gate widened with _num_splits depth, was already run as sliding-single-launch-fused-attention. That run's sliding path matches this kernel body verbatim, and the full-layer changes since then do not touch sliding shapes. So the S=16 effect can be read straight against those numbers: 23.87 -> ? at decode_16 and 38.47 -> ? at decode_32. The FA3 incumbent is in the same run as the reference. Reverting a landed hypothesis would change nothing on the sliding shapes. Results come per shape, so a loss on decode_32 alone can still be read. If decode_32 lags, the follow-up is a stacked ab-tune (S=32, one tile per program, or S=8 to fit one wave), not a companion now. Attention has only 2 checks left today, which also argues against spending one on a companion.
rules_flags: No rule problems found. The predicate is config-only (window, q_len). The new split count is a constant. There are no host syncs. ws_acc/ws_ml come from torch.empty sized from config inside kernel_fn, which is graph-safe.

The persistent ticket counters (_counters keyed on B, Hkv, device) hold no data derived from inputs: they are reset to 0 by the last-ticket program each launch. The judge accepted them at B=1 (job 295727fc68e14093) and at B=16/32 (the sliding-single-launch run). They rely on the first call per (B, Hkv) being eager, which held in both earlier runs.

Precision: q is bf16 (finer than E4M3, allowed), the cache stays E4M3 and the output is bf16. Every key: chunk s covers [lo + s*chunk, min(+chunk, seq)), the splits tile [lo, seq-1] exactly, and the new key sits in split S-1. With S=16 at small ctx (test batch 1 ctx 10, batch 3 ctx 2047), most splits are empty, which the -inf-safe combine handles. B=1 S=16 already passes this.

Test coverage: batch 3 ctx 2047 page 64 and batch 4 ctx 6000 dist edges page 1 now run the fused kernel at S=16, where the earlier run used S=8. The window-edge masking is per row and does not depend on S, so the risk is low. A sliding decode with kv_scale 1/64 is still not covered by any test (its only kv_scale sliding test is q_len 8). That gap was already present at B=1.
open_questions: At B=32, how many CTAs per SM can be resident (smem with num_stages=2 on a 2-iteration loop, plus registers)? If it is below 8, 1024 CTAs is about 1.1 waves. num_stages=1 or S=8 might fit one wave better. Read the occupancy from the profile if it is available.

Is the ~10.5 us kernel time at B=1 (32 CTAs, 2 tiles) mostly the serialized combine tail (last ticket reloads 16 partials from L2 after a gpu-scope fence)? If so, it stays fixed at large B and caps decode_16/32 near 11-13 us. The S=32 follow-up would double the combine work and may not help.
If sliding-fused-triton-decode1-splits-32 lands first, check that this branch's split-count edit still leaves B=1 at whatever S master then uses (i.e. it should only override for batch > 1).
